questions.stem: The 'Toda' tribe is primarily found in which region?
questions.explanation: The Toda are a pastoral tribe of the Nilgiri Hills in Tamil Nadu, known for their distinctive barrel-vaulted huts, buffalo herding, and embroidered shawls (putukuli). They are one of the most studied tribes in anthropology.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The 'Gond' tribe, one of the largest tribal groups in India, is concentrated mainly in which state?
questions.explanation: The Gond are one of the largest tribal communities in India, concentrated mainly in Madhya Pradesh (and Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Telangana). They are known for Gond painting, a distinctive folk art tradition. Gondwana refers historically to their region.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The 'Bhil' tribe is predominantly found in which part of India?
questions.explanation: The Bhil are one of the largest tribal groups in India, predominantly found in western and central India — Rajasthan, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, and Maharashtra. Known as skilled archers historically, they have a rich tradition of Pithora painting.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The 'Santhal' tribe, one of the largest in India, is mainly found in which region?

options.text: Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha (Chota Nagpur region)

questions.explanation: The Santhal (Santal) are one of India's largest tribes, concentrated in Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha, and Bihar (the Chota Nagpur plateau region). They led the famous Santhal Rebellion (Hul) of 1855–56 against British and zamindar oppression. They have their own script, Ol Chiki.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The 'Jarawa' and 'Sentinelese' are tribes found in which region?
questions.explanation: The Jarawa and Sentinelese are among the indigenous tribes of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. The Sentinelese (of North Sentinel Island) are one of the world's last uncontacted peoples. These are classified as Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs), and contact with them is legally restricted.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The 'Khasi' and 'Jaintia' tribes are native to which state?
questions.explanation: The Khasi, Jaintia, and Garo are the three major tribes of Meghalaya. The Khasi and Jaintia are notable for being matrilineal societies (lineage and inheritance pass through the mother, with the youngest daughter inheriting ancestral property). The state's name and culture are deeply tied to these tribes.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The matrilineal system of inheritance is a notable feature of which tribe?
questions.explanation: The Khasi tribe of Meghalaya follows a matrilineal system, where descent and inheritance pass through the female line, and the youngest daughter (Khadduh) inherits the ancestral property. The Garo of Meghalaya are also matrilineal. This contrasts with most other Indian tribes, which are patrilineal.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The 'Bodo' tribe, the largest tribal group of Assam, is associated with which autonomous region?
questions.explanation: The Bodo are the largest tribal community in Assam and are associated with the Bodoland Territorial Region (BTR), an autonomous area under the Sixth Schedule. The Bodo movement led to the 2020 Bodo Accord. Bodo is also one of the languages in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The term 'PVTG' used in the context of Indian tribes stands for:
questions.explanation: PVTG stands for Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group — a sub-category of Scheduled Tribes that are the most disadvantaged, characterised by pre-agricultural technology, low literacy, stagnant/declining population, and economic backwardness. There are 75 PVTGs in India (e.g., the Sentinelese, Jarawa, Birhor, Toda). The PM-JANMAN scheme targets their development.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Birsa Munda, a legendary tribal freedom fighter, belonged to which tribe?
questions.explanation: Birsa Munda belonged to the Munda tribe of the Chota Nagpur region (Jharkhand). He led the Ulgulan ('Great Tumult') rebellion against British rule and exploitative practices in the late 1890s. India observes 15 November (his birth anniversary) as Janjatiya Gaurav Divas (Tribal Pride Day).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The 'Apatani' tribe, known for its unique sustainable agriculture, is found in which state?
questions.explanation: The Apatani tribe inhabits the Ziro Valley of Arunachal Pradesh, renowned for their highly efficient and sustainable wet-rice cultivation integrated with fish farming. The Apatani cultural landscape is on UNESCO's tentative list of World Heritage Sites. They were historically known for facial tattoos and nose plugs (now discontinued).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The 'Warli' tribe, famous for a distinctive style of folk painting, is found mainly in which state?
questions.explanation: The Warli tribe of Maharashtra (and the Gujarat border region) is famous for Warli painting — a tribal art form using simple geometric shapes (circles, triangles, squares) in white pigment on mud walls, depicting daily life and nature. It has received a Geographical Indication (GI) tag.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which constitutional article provides for the specification of Scheduled Tribes?
questions.explanation: Article 342 empowers the President to specify the Scheduled Tribes (in consultation with the Governor), with Parliament able to modify the list. Article 341 deals with Scheduled Castes (the parallel provision). The Fifth and Sixth Schedules deal with the administration of tribal/scheduled areas.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The 'Sixth Schedule' of the Constitution provides for the administration of tribal areas in which states?
questions.explanation: The Sixth Schedule provides for the administration of tribal areas in the four northeastern states of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram, through Autonomous District Councils (ADCs) with legislative, judicial, and financial powers. The Fifth Schedule covers tribal areas in other states (like the central Indian tribal belt).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The 'Chenchu' tribe, a PVTG, is primarily found in which state?
questions.explanation: The Chenchu are an aboriginal forest-dwelling tribe (a PVTG) found primarily in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, especially around the Nallamala forests (Nagarjunsagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve). They are traditionally hunter-gatherers with deep knowledge of the forest.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The 'Munda', 'Ho', and 'Santhal' tribes predominantly speak languages belonging to which language family?
questions.explanation: The Munda, Ho, and Santhal tribes speak languages of the Austroasiatic family (specifically the Munda branch) — distinct from the Indo-Aryan and Dravidian families that dominate most of India. Santali is an Austroasiatic language included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which state has the highest proportion of Scheduled Tribe population in India?
questions.explanation: Mizoram has the highest proportion of Scheduled Tribe population among states (over 94%), followed by Nagaland and Meghalaya. Among Union Territories, Lakshadweep has the highest. In ABSOLUTE numbers, Madhya Pradesh has the largest ST population. The percentage-vs-absolute distinction is a common exam point.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The 'Great Andamanese', 'Onge', 'Jarawa', and 'Sentinelese' belong to which broad ethnic group?
questions.explanation: The Great Andamanese, Onge, Jarawa, and Sentinelese are Negrito tribes — among the oldest inhabitants of the Andaman Islands and believed to be descendants of early human migrations out of Africa. The Nicobarese and Shompen of the Nicobar Islands are of Mongoloid stock, by contrast.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The 'Gaddi' tribe, traditionally semi-nomadic shepherds, is associated with which state?
questions.explanation: The Gaddi are a semi-nomadic, transhumant pastoral tribe of Himachal Pradesh (especially the Bharmour/Chamba region), known for herding sheep and goats and migrating seasonally between the lower and higher Himalayas. The Gujjars are another pastoral group of the western Himalayan region.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The 'Forest Rights Act, 2006' is significant for tribal communities because it:

options.text: Bans all tribal people from entering forests
Transfers all forest land to private companies
Recognises and vests forest rights and occupation in forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes and other traditional forest dwellers

questions.explanation: The Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 — the Forest Rights Act — recognises and vests forest rights (including the right to live in and cultivate forest land, and community forest resource rights) in forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes and other traditional forest dwellers, correcting historical injustice from colonial-era forest laws.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Match the tribe to its state. Which pairing is INCORRECT?
questions.explanation: Option C is INCORRECT. The Santhal are concentrated in the Chota Nagpur region — Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha, and Bihar — NOT Kerala. The other pairings are correct: Toda (Nilgiris, Tamil Nadu), Bhil (Rajasthan/Gujarat/MP), Khasi (Meghalaya). Kerala's notable tribes include the Paniya, Kurichiya, and Irula.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The 'Dongria Kondh' tribe, which gained attention for its struggle to protect the Niyamgiri Hills, is found in which state?
questions.explanation: The Dongria Kondh are a PVTG of the Niyamgiri Hills in Odisha. They gained national and international attention for their successful struggle (upheld by the Supreme Court in 2013 via gram sabha consent) against bauxite mining in the Niyamgiri Hills, which they consider sacred. It became a landmark case for tribal and forest rights.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which tribe of Nagaland is associated with the practice of log-drums and was historically known for headhunting traditions (now ended)?
questions.explanation: The Konyak are a major Naga tribe of Nagaland (Mon district), historically known for headhunting (long discontinued) and their facial/hand tattoos marking valour. They are also known for log-drums and skilled craftsmanship. They participate prominently in the Hornbill Festival.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The PM-JANMAN scheme (Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan), launched in 2023, specifically targets:

options.text: The development of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs)

questions.explanation: PM-JANMAN (launched 2023) is a mission specifically targeting the socio-economic development of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs), providing basic facilities like housing, roads, water, electricity, education, and health to the most marginalised tribal communities. It complements broader tribal welfare schemes.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The key difference between the Fifth Schedule and the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution is that:

options.text: There is no difference; both apply to the same areas
The Fifth Schedule applies only to Jammu & Kashmir
The Sixth Schedule deals with language policy

The Fifth Schedule deals with scheduled/tribal areas in states other than the four northeastern ones, while the Sixth Schedule deals with tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram through Autonomous District Councils

questions.explanation: The Fifth Schedule governs the administration of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes in states OTHER than the four northeastern states (covering the central Indian tribal belt), with Tribes Advisory Councils and special Governor powers. The Sixth Schedule provides greater autonomy for tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram through Autonomous District/Regional Councils with legislative and judicial powers. This distinction is frequently tested.
questions.subject: General Knowledge
